lessons: Tonight's RG deck went 1-2 and lost both WB matches in 19 to 37 turn grinds with no late evasive finisher, so keep one late flier even when playing green.
Two WB decks went 2-0 and 2-1 against my RG deck, contradicting the guide's avoid-WB verdict; their Rebuke and Dead Weight removal won long stalls.
I cut black for five cards and played RG, going 1-2, yet the guide's best-scoring pair is BR at 58%, so keep black removal rather than cutting it.
My WB deck's grindy wins (37, 29 turns) ran on cheap removal like Dead Weight, Tribute to Hunger, Rebuke, and Smite the Monstrous, so prioritise those over early bodies.
The WU fliers deck (two Stitched Drake, Spectral Rider, Abbey Griffin, Chapel Geist, Claustrophobia) beat my WB 1-2, and my list had almost no reach or flier answers, so take some before pack 3.
Brain Weevil's second copy was a late-pack pick that made my deck, so by pack 3 the playables were thin; take removal and fliers earlier.
WU went 2-1 here with two Stitched Drakes, Spectral Rider and Claustrophobia, contradicting the guide's 1-2 WU warning: fliers plus removal and a clock still work in WU.
The guide says WB went 0-3 and to avoid it, yet seats 1 and 4 both finished 2-1, and I beat seat 1's WB 2-1, so do not write WB off.
I lost 1-2 to WG (19, 17, 13 turns) despite Claustrophobia and two Hysterical Blindness, so WU should keep its cheap two-drops and flier clock even when a stall looks likely.

Round 2 sideboarding brought in black cards Victim of Night and Trepanation Blade, which were off-colour for this UR deck and had already been cut from the notes, so check every sideboard swap against the colours you are playing.
Every match I lost ran 13 to 20 turns, so prioritise cheap removal like Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation over tempo cards, since long games favoured the opponents' card quality.
Silent Departure and Delver of Secrets were UR's best early plays, but the deck stalled against WU and RG, so pick a finisher or card advantage source over a marginal fourth creature.
Tonight contradicted the guide: WB went 2-1 for me, not 0-3, after cutting Walking Corpse and playing two Rebuke, Dead Weight, Voiceless Spirit and Falkenrath Noble for fliers.
Evasion plus removal carried my deck through 40- and 34-turn wins, so keep Unburial Rites, Ghoulcaller's Chant and a flier like Voiceless Spirit for long stalls.
My 1-2 loss to BR, with two games ending on turns 14 and 15, shows BR's early pressure beat me; block early with cheap creatures like Thraben Sentry.

Prioritize evasive finishers over filler: two 29-turn games and an 18-turn loss show my BR aggro deck had too few ways to close, so Thraben Purebloods and Rotting Fensnake should have yielded to better threats.
Stensia Bloodhall (pack 1 pick 8) and Cobbled Wings (pack 3 pick 13) were picks I cut, so after removal, take playable creatures for the curve over utility cards that never reach the deck.

Tonight's WG deck went 3-0 (6-1 in games) with Spider Spawning, Prey Upon, Ghostly Possession, Bonds of Faith and Chapel Geist, contradicting the guide's WG 49% and ground-creature warnings; removal plus fliers won.
Commit to your pair early: my pack 2 first pick Victim of Night went unused, while on-colour Prey Upon and Spider Spawning carried the 3-0 deck.
Keep 17 lands (10 Forest, 7 Plains) and four-plus flier answers: the 3-0 WG deck fit the guide's counts, though it ran two Gatstaf Shepherd and two Villagers as ground bodies.

Seat 3's UR deck held most of my blue-red core (Delver of Secrets, Moon Heron, Sensory Deprivation, Tormented Pariah, Village Ironsmith) and beat me 2-0, so check early whether a neighbour is already in your colours.
White was the strongest colour at this table (WG 3-0, WB 2-1, WU 2-1), and I never drafted it; my UR deck never found the pressure that closed games.
My games lasted 26, 40, and 34 turns with 17 lands, and I cut Blasphemous Act. In a stalled, grindy matchup, a sweeper or finisher is worth more than the 23rd spell.
